title: A KING, A HEAP, AND A LESSON

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But Israel did carry off for themselves the livestock and plunder of this city, as the Lord had instructed Joshua. So Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent heap of ruins, a desolate place to this day. He impaled the body of the king of Ai on a pole and left it there until evening. At sunset, Joshua ordered them to take the body from the pole and throw it down at the entrance of the city gate. And they raised a large pile of rocks over it, which remains to this day. — Josh 8:27-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice a quiet but important detail here: this time Israel was permitted to keep the plunder, "as the Lord had instructed." At Jericho, everything was devoted to God and taking any of it was forbidden — which is precisely where Achan fell. Now the very same kind of goods are lawful to take, because God had granted them. What was sin at Jericho was blessing at Ai. The difference was not the objects, but the command of God.

There is real wisdom in this for us. Right and wrong are not always determined by the thing itself, but by whether we act within or against God's instruction. Achan grasped at Jericho what God forbade; at Ai, Israel received freely what God gave. The lesson is to live according to God's word, receiving with gratitude what He grants and refusing to seize what He withholds. Contentment within God's boundaries guards us from Achan's fall.

Notice also that at sunset Joshua had the king's body taken down and buried, rather than left exposed overnight. This reflects the law God had given, that a body hung on a pole should not remain overnight (Deut 21:22-23). Even in judgment, God's people acted within His instructions.

That very law about a body on a "tree" is quoted in the New Testament about Jesus: "Cursed is everyone who is hung on a pole" (Gal 3:13). Christ took the curse we deserved, hanging on the cross in our place. The God who judges sin justly is the same God who, in Christ, bore that judgment Himself so that we might be redeemed and set free.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you let God's word, not just the thing itself, define what is right for you?
2. Are you content to receive what God grants and refuse what He withholds?
3. How does it move you that Christ became a curse for you, hung on the tree in your place?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me live within Your boundaries, receiving Your gifts with thanks and refusing what You withhold. Thank You that Christ bore the curse for me on the tree. Amen.
